name: Millard E. Tydings Memorial Bridge
facts: The Millard E. Tydings Memorial Bridge, named after a long‑serving Maryland senator, was dedicated by President John F. Kennedy on November 14, 1963, just eight days before his assassination.
Built between January 1962 and November 1963, the bridge spans the Susquehanna River from Cecil County to Harford County, carrying I‑95 over bluffs 200 feet above the river valley.

After closing for the first time during Hurricane Sandy on October 30, 2012, the bridge now uses all‑electronic tolling, collecting $8 northbound for autos without E‑ZPass and $6 for Maryland‑issued E‑ZPass holders.
